subject: Q2 renewal: retainer -> committed throughput & price stability request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@clearline.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q2 renewal — commit conversion and price stability request

Hi Grace,

Hope you had a good weekend. Our retainer ends at the end of May and we need to lock a renewal path. Over the last 6 months our usage has stabilized around ~1.2M tokens/month with predictable peaks up to 1.8M. We'd like to convert our existing retainer into a committed monthly throughput (targeting 1.5M tokens/month) to secure better unit economics and predictable spend.

Two asks from our side:
- A price hold at the current blended rate for 12 months if we move to a 12-month commit.
- A one-time onboarding/transition credit to cover integration and eval overhead (~$50k).

I attached our March usage export for reference. Can you confirm if Redwood can provide a commit + price hold + credits structure? If you need a phased commit (6 -> 12 months) we can discuss.

Would like to get this wrapped by May 1 to align with our finance cadence.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Data Platforms
Clearline Analytics

Attachment: usage_report_Mar2027.csv
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 renewal — commit conversion and price stability request

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the usage file. I’ll loop in Ben on pricing and Aisha (your AM) on logistics. We can absolutely explore a committed monthly throughput and a pricing stability window; I just need to confirm the numbers and internal approvals on the onboarding credit.

Ben/Aisha — tagging you in. Can we put together 2 tidy options (6m vs 12m) with credits and an overage protection mechanism that keeps their burst costs predictable? I’ll aim to get something to Elena by EOD tomorrow.

— Grace

Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Clearline renewal — quick pricing ask

Ben / Aisha — quick note on context: Clearline wants to convert a retainer into 1.5M tokens/month committed. Current blended ARR-level spend would make a 1.5M commit economically sensible for us. They are asking for a 12-month price hold and a ~$50k one-time credit. They can sign by ~May 1 if we move quickly.

Key constraints: finance prefers credit smaller than $50k or structured (credit amortized over N months). Legal wants minimal SLA change but procurement needs a clause for price rollback if usage drops below X.

Can you sketch two options I can present — 12-month and 6-month — with clearly stated credits and overage caps?

Thanks,
G
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Clearline renewal — quick pricing ask

Grace / Aisha — here are two pragmatic structures we can offer that balance economics and the customer's asks. I also attached a draft amendment (proposed_amendment_v1.pdf) to show language around commit, overage, and credits.

Option A — 12-month committed throughput (preferred):
- Commit: 1.5M tokens/month for 12 months
- Unit price: current blended rate minus 8% (conditional on 12-month signature)
- Price hold: 12 months from effective date
- Onboarding credit: $40,000 issued as a one-time invoice credit at contract execution
- Overage: capped at 20% of monthly commit at a fixed overage step rate (30% higher than committed unit price); any overage beyond 20% billed at list with alerts
- Surge credit bank: 200k token equivalent one-time credit usable within first 60 days

Option B — 6-month pilot to 12-month conversion:
- Commit: 1.0M tokens/month for 6 months, with option to convert to 1.5M for remaining 6 months
- Unit price: current blended rate minus 5% for first 6 months; conversion to 8% discount if they convert to 12m by month 4
- Onboarding credit: $20,000
- Overage: standard overage rates, with first month of conversion having a 100k token grace buffer

Notes / commercial guardrails:
- Credits amortized on Redwood invoice as single line items (Finance prefers this instead of multi-month amortization).
- Legal: include a minimum usage floor clause (40% of committed tokens) that triggers renegotiation if sustained for 2 consecutive months. This protects against deep underuse.
- SLA rollback: we can offer a price hold tied to the commit; if customer requests early termination we recoup pro-rated credits.

If we want to be more aggressive on the $50k ask we could meet them at $50k only if they sign a 24-month commitment or agree to a staged consumption minimum; I'd avoid that unless necessary.

— Ben
Finance & GTM Pricing
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_amendment_v1.pdf
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Internal: Clearline renewal — quick pricing ask

Grace — I agree with Ben's structures. A few operational asks before we send externally:
- Legal should review the minimum-usage floor and the recoup language for credits (I can spin that up today).
- Procurement typically needs DocuSign & a one-page SOW that calls out support contacts and onboarding milestones tied to the credit release.
- Suggest we include a 30-day decision cut-off to lock the price hold so their finance team has a clear deadline.

If you want, I’ll draft the SOW and route to Legal and Procurement; Ben, can you confirm the credit GL codes so Finance can pre-approve?

— Aisha
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Q2 renewal — retainer -> committed throughput & price stability request

Hi Elena — thanks again for the clear ask and for the usage file. Apologies for the back-and-forth while we pulled internal approvals — appreciate your patience. Below is a concise proposal we can put under agreement quickly. I attached a clean amendment (proposed_amendment_v3.pdf) that reflects the 12-month option (Option A) and includes the minimum-usage floor language and DocuSign placeholders.

Summary proposal (Option A, preferred):
- Commit: 1.5M tokens/month for 12 months
- Unit price: current blended rate less 8%
- Price hold: 12 months from effective date
- One-time onboarding credit: $40,000 applied as invoice credit at execution
- Surge credit: 200k token credit usable in first 60 days
- Overage protection: overage capped at 20% with fixed step-rate; alerts at 80% and 100% of commit
- Minimum usage floor: 40% of committed tokens for any 2 consecutive months triggers commercial review (protects both parties)

Next steps:
1) If that looks good, I’ll send the amendment via DocuSign and a one-page SOW that ties the $40k credit to onboarding milestones.
2) Sign by 2027-04-30 to lock the price hold and onboarding credit.

If you need a more conservative 6-month pilot path we can send Option B instead, but the best unit economics are on the 12-month path.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if Elena or finance wants to walk the numbers.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
